```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: ns-backup
  namespace: my-namespace
spec:
  schedule: 0 2 * * *
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
          - name: restic-installer
            image: alpine:3.17
            command: ['sh', '-c', 'apk add --no-cache restic']

          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

Why This Is Asked
Tests practical CKAD skills: PVCs, InitContainers, ConfigMaps, sidecars, readiness/liveness, and network policies in a realistic static content scenario.

Key Concepts
- PVC-backed volumes and ConfigMap mounts
- InitContainer for initial bootstrap
- Sidecar for live file reloads
- ConfigMap-driven content flags
- Namespace NetworkPolicy for egress control

Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: static-content-server
  namespace: ckad-demo
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: static-content
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: static-content
    spec:
      volumes:
        - name: html
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: static-content-pvc
        - name: template
          configMap:
            name: page-template
        - name: config
          configMap:
            name: page-config
      initContainers:
        - name: init
          image: alpine
          command: ["sh", "-c", "cp /template/index.html /usr/share/nginx/html/index.html"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: html
              mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html
            - name: template
              mountPath: /template
      containers:
        - name: nginx
          image: nginx:alpine
          volumeMounts:
            - name: html
              mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html
        - name: reload-agent
          image: busybox
          command: ["sh", "-c", "while true; do inotifywait -e modify /usr/share/nginx/html/index.html; nginx -s reload; done"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: html
              mountPath: /usr/share/nginx/html
      readinessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /index.html
          port: 80
        initialDelaySeconds: 5
        periodSeconds: 10
      livenessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /index.html
          port: 80
        initialDelaySeconds: 15
        periodSeconds: 20
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to compose CKAD primitives into a small, observable application with proper security and observability patterns.

## Key Concepts
- ConfigMaps and Secrets for configuration management
- InitContainers and Sidecars for application lifecycle management
- Probes (readiness and liveness) for health monitoring
- Namespace NetworkPolicy for traffic security
- RBAC basics for in-namespace metrics access
- Observability and security trade-offs in containerized applications

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal Deployment sketch
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: python-api
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: python-api
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: python-api
    spec:
      initContainers:
      - name: install-deps
        image: python:3.11-alpine
        command: ['sh', '-c', 'pip install -r /app/requirements.txt']
        volumeMounts:
        - name: app-code
          mountPath: /app
      containers:
      - name: api
        image: python:3.11-alpine
        command: ['python', '/app/main.py']
        env:
        - name: ENABLE_METRICS
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: app-config
              key: ENABLE_METRICS
        - name: API_USERNAME
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: api-credentials
              key: username
        - name: API_PASSWORD
          valueFrom:
            secretKeyRef:
              name: api-credentials
              key: password
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /health
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 20
        volumeMounts:
        - name: app-code
          mountPath: /app
      - name: cert-rotator
        image: cert-manager/cert-manager-rotator:latest
        volumeMounts:
        - name: certs
          mountPath: /etc/certs
      volumes:
      - name: app-code
        configMap:
          name: app-code
      - name: certs
        emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: restrict-egress
  namespace: target-namespace
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: monitoring
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 9000
```

## Trade-offs
- **Security vs. Complexity**: NetworkPolicy adds security but increases deployment complexity
- **Resource Overhead**: Sidecar containers double resource requirements for cert management
- **Observability Cost**: Metrics endpoint requires additional monitoring infrastructure
- **InitContainer Impact**: Dependency installation extends pod startup time
- **Namespace Isolation**: Per-namespace design improves security boundaries but requires duplicate configuration management

## Why This Is Asked
Tests CKAD ability to compose a small, namespace-scoped verification workflow that touches ConfigMaps, Secrets, PVCs, and network policy.

## Key Concepts
- Deployment with InitContainer
- ConfigMap-based allowlist
- Secret-based credentials and TLS sidecar
- PVC-mounted /secrets and lightweight parsing with jq/yq
- Readiness/Liveness probes and per-namespace NetworkPolicy

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: compliance-api-creds
  namespace: default
data:
  token: <base64>
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: secret-allowlist
  namespace: default
data:
  allowed_keys: |
    tls.key
    tls.crt
    creds
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: secret-compliance-checker
  namespace: default
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: secret-compliance-checker
    spec:
      initContainers:
        - name: install-tools
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["sh", "-c", "apk add --no-cache jq curl && wget -O - https://github.com/yq-dev/yq/releases/latest/download/yq_linux_amd64 -O /usr/local/bin/yq && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq"]
      containers:
        - name: checker
          image: alpine:3.18
          command: ["/bin/sh", "-c", "./check.sh"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: secrets
              mountPath: /secrets
      volumes:
        - name: secrets
          persistentVolumeClaim:
            claimName: secret-storage
      readinessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /healthz
          port: 8080
        initialDelaySeconds: 5
        periodSeconds: 10
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you scale and test this in a real cluster?
- What are risks with mounting Secrets in /secrets and how to mitigate?

## Why This Is Asked
This checks secure defaults and practical CKAD patterns: ConfigMap/Secret usage, correct SecurityContext, and health checks.

## Key Concepts
- SecurityContext: runAsNonRoot, runAsUser, readOnlyRootFilesystem, capabilities: drop: ALL

## Code Example
```yaml
# Minimal Deployment skeleton (yaml)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: flask-app
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: flask-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: flask-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: flask
        image: python:3.11-slim
        command: ["python", "/app/main.py"]
        volumeMounts:

          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 10
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz

          initialDelaySeconds: 15

            memory: "128Mi"
          limits:
            cpu: "200m"
            memory: "256Mi"

      - name: app-config
        configMap:
          name: flask-config
      - name: api-key
        secret:
          secretName: flask-api-key
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests RBAC scoping, CronJob scheduling, and in-cluster data backup to a ConfigMap without leaking secrets.

## Key Concepts
- RBAC granularity scoped to a namespace
- CronJob scheduling and Job templates
- Reading Kubernetes events via API in-cluster
- Updating/creating a ConfigMap from a Job

## Code Example

```yaml
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: events-backup-sa
  namespace: metrics
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: events-backup-role
  namespace: metrics
rules:
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["events"]
  verbs: ["get","list","watch"]
- apiGroups: [""]
  resources: ["configmaps"]
  verbs: ["get","update","create","patch"]
---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: RoleBinding
metadata:
  name: events-backup-binding
  namespace: metrics
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: Role
  name: events-backup-role
subjects:
- kind: ServiceAccount

  namespace: metrics
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: events-backup
```

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: data-qa-cronjob
  namespace: example
spec:
  schedule: "0 2 * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
          - name: install-deps
            image: python:3.9-alpine
            command:
            - sh
            - -c
            - |
              pip install pandas==1.3.3 jsonschema==3.2.0 --target /app/deps
            volumeMounts:
            - name: deps-volume
              mountPath: /app/deps
          containers:
          - name: validator
            image: python:3.9-alpine
            command:
            - python
            - -c
            - |
              import sys
              sys.path.append('/app/deps')
              import os
              import pandas as pd
              import jsonschema
              import requests
              from datetime import datetime
              
              schema_path = os.getenv('SCHEMA_PATH', '/data/schema.json')
              date_range = os.getenv('DATE_RANGE', '7')
              
              # Load schema
              with open(schema_path) as f:
                  schema = json.load(f)
              
              # Validate CSVs
              for csv_file in os.listdir('/data'):
                  if csv_file.endswith('.csv'):
                      df = pd.read_csv(f'/data/{csv_file}')
                      try:
                          jsonschema.validate(df.to_dict('records'), schema)
                          result = {'file': csv_file, 'status': 'pass', 'timestamp': datetime.utcnow().isoformat()}
                      except Exception as e:
                          result = {'file': csv_file, 'status': 'fail', 'error': str(e), 'timestamp': datetime.utcnow().isoformat()}
                      
                      # Send to QA portal
                      requests.post('http://qa-portal:8090/api/v1/qa', 
                                   json=result,
                                   headers={'Authorization': f"Bearer {os.getenv('QA_TOKEN')}"})

            - configMapRef:
                name: app-config
            - secretRef:
                name: qa-credentials
            volumeMounts:
            - name: data-volume
              mountPath: /data
            - name: deps-volume
              mountPath: /app/deps
              readOnly: true
            readinessProbe:
              exec:
                command:
                - python
                - -c
                - "import pandas, jsonschema, requests"
              initialDelaySeconds: 10
              periodSeconds: 5
            livenessProbe:
              exec:
                command:
                - python
                - -c
                - "import sys; sys.exit(0)"
              initialDelaySeconds: 30
              periodSeconds: 30
          - name: cert-rotator
            image: cert-manager/cert-manager-rotator:v1.8.0
            args:
            - --watch-cert-dir=/certs
            - --cert-secret-name=qa-tls-cert

            - name: cert-volume

spec:
```

## Trade-offs

**CronJob vs Deployment**: CronJob provides scheduled execution but lacks continuous monitoring. A Deployment could run continuously but would require external coordination.

**InitContainer Pattern**: Ensures dependencies are available but increases startup time and complexity. Using a pre-built image would be faster but reduces flexibility.

**Sidecar for TLS**: Separates concerns and enables independent updates but adds resource overhead and coordination complexity.

**NetworkPolicy Restriction**: Enhances security but requires careful rule management and monitoring to avoid blocking legitimate traffic.

**PVC for Data**: Ensures persistence across runs but creates coupling between namespaces and requires careful capacity planning.

## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates CKAD proficiency in extending namespace-centric validation using core Kubernetes primitives: ConfigMaps, Secrets, CronJobs, InitContainers, PVCs, and NetworkPolicies. It also tests knowledge of jq for in-cluster JSON Schema validation and idempotent status updates.

## Key Concepts

- **Namespace-scoped configuration**: All resources operate within a single namespace boundary
- **CronJob with InitContainer tooling**: InitContainer prepares the environment (curl/jq) before the main validation container runs
- **JSON Schema validation using jq**: jq processes ConfigMap data against the fetched schema
- **PVC-backed logging**: Persistent storage preserves logs across job executions
- **NetworkPolicy egress control**: Restricts outbound traffic to only approved endpoints
- **Status persistence in ConfigMap**: Validation results are stored for auditing and downstream consumption

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: ns-config-schema-validator
  namespace: <target-namespace>
spec:
  schedule: "*/7 * * * *"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          initContainers:
          - name: installer
            image: busybox
            command: ["sh", "-c", "wget -O /usr/local/bin/jq https://github.com/jqlang/jq/releases/download/jq-1.7/jq-linux64 && chmod +x /usr/local/bin/jq"]
            volumeMounts:
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /usr/local/bin
          containers:
          - name: validator
            image: curlimages/curl:latest
            env:
            - name: API_KEY
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: validation-creds
                  key: api-key
            command: ["sh", "-c"]
            args:
            - |
              SCHEMA_URL=$(kubectl get configmap validation-config -o jsonpath='{.data.schema-url}')
              curl -s $SCHEMA_URL -o /logs/schema.json
              for cm in $(kubectl get configmaps -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.name}'); do
                kubectl get configmap $cm -o json | jq -s ".[0] * {data: .[1] | getpath($cm | split(\"-\")[1:] | map(.))}" /logs/schema.json > /logs/validation-$cm.json || true
              done
              curl -X POST http://validation-portal:8080/api/v1/validate -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" --data-binary @/logs/summary.json
            volumeMounts:
            - name: logs
              mountPath: /logs
            - name: tools
              mountPath: /usr/local/bin
          volumes:
          - name: logs
            persistentVolumeClaim:
              claimName: validation-logs
          - name: tools
            emptyDir: {}
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

## Trade-offs

| Aspect | Trade-off |
|--------|-----------|
| **InitContainer vs. Custom Image** | InitContainer adds startup latency but keeps the main image lightweight and avoids maintenance of a custom image. |
| **jq Validation vs. Dedicated Validator** | jq is lightweight and universally available, but lacks full JSON Schema draft support. A dedicated validator (e.g., kubeconform) offers better accuracy at the cost of added complexity. |
| **PVC for Logs** | Provides durability and debugging capability but introduces storage overhead and potential bottlenecks in high-frequency runs. |
| **NetworkPolicy Egress** | Restricts access to only required endpoints, enhancing security but requires careful planning of all dependencies. |
| **ConfigMap Status vs. Custom Resource** | ConfigMap is simpler and requires no CRD management, but lacks built-in versioning and conflict resolution. |
